summary: Iteration 41 — Iron Rabbit Persistent Cook Session + Recipe Notes After Cook tested end-to-end via live Playwright. Notes-after-Cook feature (T8/T9/T10/T11) is 100% working — prompt appears, textarea, disabled Save until non-whitespace, Save persists (cap-20 rolling log, latest shown on row with Sparkles icon), Skip skips cleanly, cook_count increments in both paths, session cleared on completion. Persistent Cook Session save (T1), resume-step-index (T2 step counter), resume-hint on Recipes list (T5), and clear-on-close-via-X (T7) all PASS. However TWO BUGS found: (BUG1 – HIGH) Timer state (ends_at / paused_remaining) is NOT actually resumed — it is immediately clobbered to null on modal mount. Root cause: React.StrictMode (enabled in /app/frontend/src/index.js) double-invokes the [idx] reset effect; the `stepChangeMountRef` guard is flipped to false by the first invocation, then the second invocation runs the body and clears endsAt / pausedRemaining. Visible symptom: reopen a paused/running session → step index correct and 'Resumed at step N' toast shows, but the button is Start (not Resume) and the timer displays the full step minutes (15:00) instead of remaining time. (BUG2 – deviates from spec) T4: opening Cook Mode on Recipe B while a session for A exists OVERWRITES A's session with B's state (persistence effect runs on mount for whichever recipe is opened). Spec explicitly said 'session for A is untouched — verify localStorage still has A's recipe_id'.

ui_bugs.issue: Timer state (endsAt, pausedRemaining) is cleared on resume because React.StrictMode double-invokes the [idx] effect. First invocation flips stepChangeMountRef.current=false and returns; StrictMode's re-invocation then runs the reset body → setEndsAt(null), setPausedRemaining(null). Result: 'Resumed at step N' toast + step index resume WORK, but timer resume is silently broken — Start (not Resume) button shows and remaining time is lost.

Opening Cook Mode on Recipe B while a session exists for Recipe A immediately overwrites the saved session with B's step_idx=0 state on mount. Spec required A's session to remain untouched. Behavior conflicts with the resume-hint semantics (session for A silently lost the moment user peeks at B).

Confirms StrictMode-double-invocation bug.

action_items: FIX BUG1 (HIGH): Replace the useRef mount-guard in CookModeModal step-reset effect (L655-666) with an idx-value guard so it survives React.StrictMode's double effect invocation. Suggested pattern: `const prevIdxRef = useRef(idx); useEffect(() => { if (prevIdxRef.current === idx) return; prevIdxRef.current = idx; /* reset logic */ }, [idx]);`. This makes the effect idempotent — StrictMode's re-invocation is a no-op because prevIdx already equals idx after the first run. Without this fix, timer resume is silently broken in dev/StrictMode environments and any React 19+ StrictMode-strict environment.

FIX BUG2 (MEDIUM) — spec deviation: When opening Cook Mode for a DIFFERENT recipe than the saved session's recipe_id, do NOT immediately overwrite the saved session with the new recipe's state. Options: (a) delay first saveCookSession until user interacts (click Next / Start), or (b) skip persistence entirely when the current recipe.id !== savedSession?.recipe_id and idx===0 && endsAt===null && pausedRemaining===null (i.e. clean-start state).

Optional: The 'Resumed at step N' toast fires up to 4× per resume due to React 18 StrictMode + re-mounts triggered by parent state changes. Toast dedupe on toast.success ID (`toast.success(..., { id:'rg-resume' })`) would silence duplicates.
critical_code_review_comments: React.StrictMode is enabled globally (index.js:9). Any use of useRef({ current: true }) as a 'first-invocation-only' guard is broken by design in StrictMode. All such guards in the codebase should switch to a value-comparison guard (as in the fix above).

saveCookSession persistence effect writes on EVERY [recipe.id, idx, endsAt, pausedRemaining] change, including the very first mount. This is why opening Cook Mode on a fresh recipe wipes the session for another recipe. If single-session-globally is the intended model, the resume-hint UX becomes misleading because merely peeking at Recipe B destroys Recipe A's progress.

pauseTimer() `if (!endsAt) return;` silently no-ops when timer wasn't actually running — combined with BUG1 this makes the resumed-timer + pause flow completely dead. Once BUG1 is fixed this early return is fine.
RestaurantWorkspacesP6.jsx is now 1129 lines — still well above the 700-line threshold. CookModeModal (~370 lines) is a natural extraction candidate (own file + own tests).
addRecipeCookNote caps notes at 20 correctly (slice(-20)) and truncates each note to 400 chars. Clean, atomic writes. Nice.
Note prompt uses `disabled={!noteDraft.trim()}` — correct (whitespace-only cannot be saved). autoFocus on textarea is good UX.

success_rate.frontend: 9/13 (T1, T5, T6, T7, T8, T9, T10, T11 PASS; T2 partial-pass; T3 FAIL; T4 partial-pass — B fresh but A overwritten). Notes-after-Cook feature 100% passes; Persistent Session step+hint+finish clearing works, timer-state resume broken.

Session was seeded/cleared via localStorage.setItem('rg_cook_session', ...) / removeItem.
context_for_next_testing_agent: React.StrictMode double-invocation is active in dev. The `stepChangeMountRef` guard in CookModeModal doesn't survive it — first invocation flips ref false and returns, second invocation runs the reset body. Anywhere else in the codebase using `useRef(true)` as a 'first-mount only' guard has the same latent bug. When retesting: (1) reopen a session with a FUTURE ends_at and confirm timer displays remaining time (not stepMinutes) and pause button (not start) is visible; (2) confirm opening a DIFFERENT recipe does not overwrite saved session (only user action inside cook mode should). Seed pattern: bootstrap stores by opening Recipes modal, then put records directly to IndexedDB IronRabbit DB — rg_restaurants + rg_recipes stores use out-of-line keys. Onboarding tour must be dismissed before opening dashboard: set ['onboardingComplete','tourComplete','hasSeenTour','onboarding_done','welcomeShown'] to 'true' in localStorage then reload.
rca of the issue: BUG1 RCA — File /app/frontend/src/notes/rg/RestaurantWorkspacesP6.jsx L655-666. Pattern used: `const stepChangeMountRef = useRef(true); useEffect(() => { if (stepChangeMountRef.current) { stepChangeMountRef.current = false; return; } /* reset endsAt & pausedRemaining */ }, [idx]);`. In React.StrictMode (enabled in index.js), useEffect body is invoked, then its cleanup is run, then the body is invoked a SECOND time — but useRef values persist across the simulated remount. So run #1 flips the ref to false, run #2 sees ref=false and executes the reset body → setEndsAt(null), setPausedRemaining(null). Reproduction: (a) seed localStorage.rg_cook_session with ends_at 2 min in future; (b) open Recipes modal; (c) click recipe-cook-mode-<id>; (d) observe cook-mode-timer-display shows step minutes (e.g. 15:00) instead of remaining ~2:00 and Start button (not Pause) — session in localStorage now has ends_at:null. Mitigation: swap the mount-guard for an idx-value guard (`prevIdxRef.current === idx` short-circuit) which is idempotent under StrictMode. BUG2 RCA — persistence useEffect L637-644 runs on mount regardless of whether the recipe matches the saved session; opening a new recipe writes {recipe_id: newId, step_idx:0, ends_at:null, paused_remaining:null}, obliterating any pre-existing session. Mitigation: only persist after user interaction, OR bail out when session state is 'clean-start' for a different recipe than what's saved.
